# Minimal HTTP health service

Origin: operator-authored architecture-prototype demonstration input. This is not an original teacher document or a formal benchmark trial.

Build a small stateless Node.js 22 HTTP service using only built-in http and node:test. No database, Docker, identity provider, third-party packages or cloud infrastructure is required.

FR1: GET /health returns HTTP 200 and JSON {"status":"ok"}.
FR2: Unknown routes return HTTP 404 and a JSON error. After an unknown request the service must still answer /health.
FR3: npm start listens on process.env.PORT, default 3000. Keep the exported application/server factory separate from the executable startup file so tests do not start an uncontrolled fixed-port server.
NFR1: npm test runs real HTTP tests on an ephemeral loopback port, checking health, unknown route and health again; close the server after testing. Do not replace actual HTTP behavior with mocks.
NFR2: npm run build checks all source JavaScript syntax. Deliver package.json, source, tests and README with install/start/test instructions and a small source-to-requirement mapping. Keep consistent CommonJS conventions with .cjs source files.

# Health service structure

Origin: operator-authored architecture-prototype demonstration input.

```plantuml
@startuml
actor Client
component "Startup entry" as Startup
component "Exported HTTP server factory" as Application
component "Real ephemeral-port tests" as Tests
Startup --> Application : create and listen on PORT
Tests --> Application : create and listen on loopback random port
Client --> Application : GET /health or unknown route
@enduml
```

{"path": "architecture-decisions.md", "content": "# Architecture Decisions

## AD-1: Minimal library-like service, no external runtime dependencies
The design mandates only built-in `http` and `node:test`. We use no third-party packages, no database, no Docker, no identity provider, no cloud infrastructure. This keeps the repository small and runnable on Node.js 22 with zero `npm install` network fetches beyond the Node runtime.

## AD-2: Separate exported server factory from the executable startup entry
FR1/FR2 state the HTTP behavior; FR3 explicitly requires the application/server factory to be separate from the startup file so tests do not spawn an uncontrolled fixed-port server. We implement:

- `src/app.cjs` — exports `createServer()` (derived name, see assumptions) returning an `http.Server` with the request handler; it never calls `listen`.
- `src/server.cjs` — imports the factory, reads `process.env.PORT` (default 3000), and calls `listen`.

This directly mirrors the PlantUML view: Startup → Application ("create and listen on PORT") and Tests → Application ("create and listen on loopback random port").

## AD-3: Stateless request handler
The handler matches only `GET /health` (200 JSON `{"status":"ok"}`) and returns 404 JSON for every other route. No mutable state is kept, guaranteeing FR2's requirement that `/health` still answers correctly after an unknown request.

## AD-4: Real HTTP tests on an ephemeral port
NFR1 forbids mocks. Tests import the factory, listen on loopback `127.0.0.1:0`, use Node's built-in HTTP client (`http.get`) to assert health → unknown → health, and close the server in an `after()` hook. Port 0 lets the OS assign a free ephemeral port in every run.

## AD-5: Syntax-check build without third-party tooling
NFR2 requires `npm run build` to check all source JavaScript syntax. Since third-party linters are disallowed, `scripts/check-syntax.cjs` invokes `node --check` on each `.cjs` source file and fails on any non-zero exit.

## AD-6: CommonJS `.cjs` conventions
NFR2 requires consistent CommonJS with `.cjs` source files. All source and test files use `.cjs` and `module.exports`/`require`."}

{"path": "README.md", "content": "# Minimal HTTP health service

A small, stateless Node.js 22 HTTP service built only with the built-in `http` and `node:test` modules. No database, Docker, identity provider, third-party packages, or cloud infrastructure is required.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22+

## Install

There are no third-party dependencies, so no install step is required. The project uses consistent CommonJS conventions with `.cjs` source files.

```sh
npm install   # optional; resolves to nothing beyond the runtime
```

## Start

```sh
npm start
```

`npm start` listens on `process.env.PORT`, defaulting to `3000`:

```sh
PORT=8080 npm start
```

## Test

```sh
npm test
```

`npm test` runs real HTTP tests (`node --test`) against an ephemeral loopback port. The tests hit `/health`, an unknown route, and `/health` again, then close the server. HTTP behavior is exercised directly — no mocks.

## Build / syntax check

```sh
npm run build
```

`npm run build` syntax-checks all source JavaScript (`scripts/check-syntax.cjs`), which runs `node --check` over each `.cjs` source file.

## Routes

| Route              | Method | Status | Body                          |
| ------------------ | ------ | ------ | ----------------------------- |
| `/health`          | GET    | 200    | `{"status":"ok"}`             |
| any other route    | any    | 404    | JSON error (e.g. `{"error":"Not Found"}`) |

## Source to requirement mapping

| Requirement | Description                                                            | Source / test                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| FR1         | `GET /health` returns HTTP 200 and JSON `{"status":"ok"}`             | `src/app.cjs` · `test/health.test.cjs`     |
| FR2         | Unknown routes return HTTP 404 + JSON error; `/health` still answers  | `src/app.cjs` · `test/health.test.cjs`     |
| FR3         | `npm start` listens on `process.env.PORT` (default 3000); factory kept separate from startup | `src/server.cjs` · `src/app.cjs`           |
| NFR1        | `npm test` runs real HTTP tests on an ephemeral loopback port          | `test/health.test.cjs`                     |
| NFR2        | `npm run build` checks all source syntax; CommonJS `.cjs` conventions  | `scripts/check-syntax.cjs` · `package.json` |

## Layout

```
package.json              scripts (start, test, build)
scripts/check-syntax.cjs  node --check over source files
src/app.cjs               handler + exported server factory (Application)
src/server.cjs            executable startup entry (Startup)
test/health.test.cjs      real ephemeral-port HTTP tests (Tests)
```"}
